This one points to a pretty nasty problem with `EditorFileSystem::_scan_filesystem`, where it calls `ResourceUID::clear` as part of the _threaded_ scan, which first of all is not covered by a mutex, so is presumably opening us up to race conditions (and thus random crashes) if it gets called while something else is mutating something like `ResourceUID::unique_ids`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/944a3c6cbbbb88284feebcb0603464cb175fa18e/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L513-L514

Here's the call stack for that call:

```
ResourceUID::clear() (core/io/resource_uid.cpp:408)
EditorFileSystem::_scan_filesystem() (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:514)
EditorFileSystem::_thread_func(void*) (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:558)
Thread::callback(unsigned long, Thread::Settings const&, void (*)(void*), void*) (core/os/thread.cpp:64)
```

With the thread having been started here:

```
EditorFileSystem::scan() (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:1137)
EditorNode::_notification(int) (editor/editor_node.cpp:962)
EditorNode::_notification_forwardv(int) (editor/editor_node.h:123)
Object::_notification_forward(int) (core/object/object.cpp:874)
Object::notification(int, bool) (core/object/object.h:727)
SceneTree::_process_group(SceneTree::ProcessGroup*, bool) (scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1236)
SceneTree::_process(bool) (scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1313)
SceneTree::process(double) (scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:719)
Main::iteration() (main/main.cpp:5017)
OS_LinuxBSD::run() (platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:1000)
main (platform/linuxbsd/godot_linuxbsd.cpp:122)
```

That `ResourceUID::clear` ends up clearing the entry for our main scene, which was already added beforehand, here:

```
ResourceUID::add_id(long, String const&) (core/io/resource_uid.cpp:158)
EditorFileSystem::_scan_for_uid_directory(EditorFileSystem::ScannedDirectory const*, HashSet<String, HashMapHasherDefault, HashMapComparatorDefault<String, void>> const&) (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:308)
EditorFileSystem::scan_for_uid() (editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp:278)
ResourceUID::get_id_path(long) const (core/io/resource_uid.cpp:203)
Main::start() (main/main.cpp:4302)
main (platform/linuxbsd/godot_linuxbsd.cpp:121)
```

So the fundamental problem seems to be that we are calling `ResourceUID::ensure_path` in a bunch of places that can potentially run during the threaded `EditorFileSystem` scan, like `EditorAudioBuses::_server_save` or `FileSystemDock::_project_settings_changed`, where the UIDs have all been cleared and are still in the process of being populated, on a separate thread.

I'm not entirely sure what the best fix is, but clearing out the entire UID cache as part of the scan seems very aggressive. Some kind of double-buffering might be a better approach. If that's problematic then the places calling `ResourceUID::ensure_path` needs some kind of graceful failure, or we shouldn't really allow anything else to happen during a scan in the first place.
